title: The day a drill bit pulled the plug on a lake (Lake Peigneur, 1980)

lines: In 1980, one drill bit pulled the plug on an entire lake.

lines.text: Lake Peigneur, Louisiana. Ten feet deep, with an oil rig drilling in the middle.
lines.say: Lake Pain-yer, Louisiana. Ten feet deep, with an oil rig drilling in the middle.

lines: But under the lake sat a salt mine, with fifty-five miners inside.
At twelve hundred feet, the drill punched right through its roof.
The lake poured in and started to spin. It swallowed the rig, eleven barges and a tugboat.
The canal from the sea ran backwards, into a one hundred sixty-four foot waterfall. And every miner got out alive.
So why a whirlpool, not just a drain?
Water always carries a little spin. Pulled inward, speed times radius stays the same. Half the distance, double the speed.
And fresh water eats salt. Every cubic meter can dissolve about three hundred fifty kilos, so the hole kept growing.
It's your bathtub drain, with a salt mine at the bottom.
